label: Person
name: Juan Gil de Hontañón
summary:
Juan Gil de Hontañón was a master builder and Trasmeran mason of Spain during the 16th century. Born in Rasines in 1480, he is best known for his work on the Isabelline Gothic Segovia Cathedral, the Castle of Turégano, various monasteries, and the Cathedral of Palencia.

His association with the school of Juan Guas marked a significant turning point in his career, leading to numerous commissions across Spain. Hontañón's innovative use of ashlar masonry and his emphasis on structural integrity have had a lasting impact on Spanish architecture.

As one of the most prominent architects of his time, Hontañón's work continues to be studied by historians and architects today, offering valuable insights into the artistic and cultural landscape of 16th-century Spain.

In his later years, Hontañón was appointed as the royal architect for King Charles I of Spain, overseeing several major projects across the kingdom.
